name: People counted as homeless
definition: Total people experiencing homelessness on one night in January (sheltered in emergency shelter, safe havens or transitional housing, plus unsheltered), HUD point-in-time count for the New York City Continuum of Care (NY-600).

source.name: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, CoC Homeless Populations and Subpopulations reports, NY-600 New York City CoC, 2007-2025

peers.note: Total homeless persons per 10,000 residents, January 2025 count, for the Continuum of Care that contains each city. CoC boundaries do not match city limits: most cover a whole county or several counties, so the denominator is the Census Vintage 2025 (July 1, 2025) population of the area the CoC covers, as described in each row. Where a CoC's exact boundary differs from its name (for example Dallas also covers Collin County) the area used is stated; the rates are approximate and depend on each CoC's own counting method, especially for the unsheltered count. Large-shelter right-to-shelter cities such as New York count far more sheltered people than cities without that obligation.

source.name: HUD CoC Homeless Populations and Subpopulations reports, 2025; Census Bureau Vintage 2025 county and city population estimates

method: For each year, downloaded HUD's Homeless Populations and Subpopulations PDF for NY-600 and read the 'Total Homeless Persons' row (2007-2011 reports label it 'Total Homeless Persons in Households'). A value was accepted only if emergency shelter + transitional housing + unsheltered equals the printed total. Count dates: 2007 1/29/2007, 2008 1/28/2008, 2009 1/26/2009, 2010 1/25/2010, 2011 1/31/2011, 2012 1/30/2012, 2014 1/27/2014, 2015 2/9/2015, 2017 2/7/2017, 2018 1/22/2018, 2019 1/28/2019, 2020 1/27/2020, 2021 1/26/2021, 2022 1/25/2022, 2023 1/24/2023, 2024 1/23/2024, 2025 1/28/2025. No report could be downloaded for 2013, 2016.
caveats: HUD's preferred download, the 'PIT Counts by CoC' workbook on huduser.gov, refused automated requests and is in .xlsb format; these per-year CoC reports carry the same counts as submitted by the CoC.
No value for 2013, 2016: HUD's report for those years could not be found at its usual address. They are left out, not estimated.
2021: HUD let communities cancel or modify the unsheltered count because of COVID-19; HUD's report warns that unsheltered and total counts for 2021 may be incomplete.
Most of New York's count is people in shelter: in January 2025, 118,160 in emergency shelter, 2,850 in transitional housing and 4,673 unsheltered, per HUD's report.
The count is one night in January, not the number of people homeless over a year.
